hints.content:
The function $g$ is negative $($i.e. $g(x)<0)$ whenever its graph is below the $x$-axis.

This is because the negative $y$-values are below the $x$-axis, and $y=g(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by one-half. The graph of the function y equals g of x is above the x-axis from x equals negative five to x equals negative three and three-quarters. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative three and three-quarters to x equals negative one. It is above the x-axis from x equals negative one to x equals one. It is below the x-axis from x equals one to x equals three and three-quarters. It is above the x-axis after x equals three and three-quarters. The function decreases from x equals negative five to x equals negative three. It increases from x equals negative three to x equals zero. It decreases from x equals zero to x equals three. It increases after x equals three. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative three and three-quarters to x equals negative one and from x equals one to x equals three and three-quarters.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $2<x<3$.
